title: fast-track plan-ready: issues derivados e suggestions pulam o grill
description:
PROBLEMA: o redesign do issue-system (CAM-106/107) cravou o grill como o gate humano singular: stage idea -> specified so via /cam-spec (issue-specify.ts:368), e o gate de plannability chaveia em stage===specified em 3 lugares (select.ts:34, rank.ts:154, gate.ts:150). Mas grill e UMA porta pra plan-readiness, nao a unica. Alguns issues nascem settled e grillar e cerimonia sem ganho de informacao: fixes derivados de root-cause concreto (CAM-142, CAM-143), SUGGESTIONs de reviewer com file:line, nice-to-haves de implementacao obvia. Exemplo real desta sessao: o CAM-142 (idea-stage) foi spec-quality no proprio issue e foi direto pro /cam-plan com so o D2 warning. Queremos um caminho de primeira classe pra isso, aplicando o grill onde ele realmente importa.

MODELO: PRD-readiness tem DUAS portas (grillado OU born-ready). A marcacao nasce no FILING (cam issue --file-local), nao no spec, porque o ponto e pular o spec. O orquestrador ja sabe quando fila um derivado (CAM-143 nasceu do dogfood do CAM-142; SUGGESTIONs de reviewer idem), entao da pra AUTO-marcar nesses caminhos.

FORK DE DESIGN (a decidir no grill): 
  Opcao X (flag, stage continua idea): { stage: idea, grillExempt: true }. Predicado vira (specified || grillExempt) && open && !blocked nos 3 sites. Honesto (nao foi grillado), mas espalha logica em 3 lugares.
  Opcao Y (filar direto em specified + discriminador): { stage: specified, specSource: grill|derived|operator }. Os 3 gates e o ranking NAO mudam (continuam chavando em specified). Redefine specified de 'grillado' para 'plan-ready'; o spec do derivado = a propria description (root-cause + fix-direction). Menos invasivo, mais limpo conceitualmente, mas muda o significado de specified e a linha do /cam-plan 'nao re-litigar o spec grillado'. Lean atual do orquestrador: Y.

GUARDRAILS (pra nao virar atalho de rigor): (1) exempt e opt-in, nunca default (issue normal continua nascendo idea/nao-exempt em alloc.ts:95); (2) exigir description nao-vazia quando exempt (o spec-equivalente tem que existir); (3) proveniencia obrigatoria: derivedFrom: 'CAM-NNN' ou origin enum, pra auditar abuso do fast-track; (4) o auditor do /cam-plan (Step 8) continua sendo o backstop: fast-track pula o grill, NAO pula a auditoria do PRD.

WRINKLE DE INTEGRACAO (o ponto que mais exige decisao): wsjf/rank hoje sao OUTPUT do grill (escritos por specifyIssueOnMain). Issue fast-track entra na fila de ranking sem passar pelo grill, entao precisa de regra: wsjf minimo no filing, OU rank default (ex: derivado herda urgencia do pai, ou ordena apos os grillados). rank.ts:154 e gate.ts:150 filtram em specified hoje.

TOUCH POINTS: scripts/cam/issues.schema.json (novo campo opcional: grillExempt/specSource + derivedFrom/origin), src/issues/select.ts:34 + src/issues/rank.ts:154 + src/issues/gate.ts:150 (predicado/redefinicao), src/issues/alloc.ts:95 (default de stage no filing), src/commands/issue-file.ts (flag --fast-track/--derived-from + auto-marcacao), .claude/commands/cam-plan.md:82 (suprimir D2 quando exempt + spec-source = description pra derivado), .claude/commands/cam-spec.md (inalterado, continua o caminho do grill), subagent-planner (spec source = description pro derivado).

PROCESSO: este issue DEVE ser grillado (revisa a decisao deliberada do CAM-107 'grill e o gate singular'; e hard-to-reverse, surpreendente sem contexto e tem trade-off real => passa nos 3 gates de ADR do projeto, escrever ADR em docs/adr/). Open questions pro grill settlar: fork X vs Y; regra de wsjf/rank pra fast-track; quem pode setar exempt (so orquestrador/operator? auto em filings de SUGGESTION/derivado?); escopo da auto-marcacao. Relacionado: CAM-106/107/108/109 (redesign do issue-system), CAM-142/143 (exemplos de derivados que nasceram plan-ready).

spec.scope: Introduce a grill-exempt fast-track so issues born plan-ready (fixes derived from other issues, reviewer suggestions, operator nice-to-haves) reach /cam-plan WITHOUT the grill, while the grill stays the path for ambiguous/greenfield ideas. Representation = Option Y: such issues are filed directly at stage:specified with a specSource discriminator; specified is redefined as "plan-ready" (grill is one path, not the only one). The 3 plannability filter sites and the ranker are UNCHANGED. IN SCOPE: schema field(s) + hard validation, the cam issue --file-local filing flags, WSJF-at-filing with parent-inheritance, /cam-plan spec-sourcing by specSource, hard guardrails, the first docs/adr ADR, and tests. OUT OF SCOPE: a reviewer-SUGGESTION auto-filer (separate follow-up issue that CONSUMES this fast-track), any content-heuristic auto-marking, and editing the vendored grilling/domain-modeling skills (that recommendation-quality clause is CAM-145, in the cam-owned wrapper).
acceptanceCriteria: Schema (issues.schema.json): specSource enum "grill"|"derived"|"operator" is REQUIRED on every stage:specified issue (total discriminator); an absent specSource on a pre-existing specified issue is treated as "grill" (back-compat). [oracle: schema validation test]

Schema: derivedFrom is string[] with minItems>=1 REQUIRED (if/then conditional) when specSource==="derived", and empty/absent otherwise; description is non-empty REQUIRED when specSource in {derived, operator}. [oracle: schema validation test]

Representation = Y: the 3 plannability filter sites (src/issues/select.ts:34, src/issues/rank.ts:154, src/issues/gate.ts:150) and the ranker keep keying on stage==="specified" and are NOT modified. [oracle: reviewer-judgment + grep no-change on the predicate]

cam issue --file-local accepts --fast-track (=> specSource:operator) and --derived-from CAM-NNN[,CAM-MMM] (=> specSource:derived + derivedFrom), filing the issue directly at stage:specified; default filing with no flag stays stage:idea (alloc.ts:95 default untouched). [oracle: filing-path test]

WSJF is resolved at filing: explicit scores accepted; when --derived-from is given and scores are omitted, a suggested WSJF is inherited from the parent issue (overridable); filing REFUSES with a clear error + non-zero exit when WSJF is unresolvable (no explicit scores and no parent-with-wsjf). [oracle: filing-path test]

All 4 guardrails are enforced HARD pre-commit (JSON-schema if/then + filing-path validation, mirroring specifyIssueOnMain): specSource-required, derivedFrom-when-derived, description-non-empty-when-fast-track, WSJF-resolvable. The ranker missing-wsjf sort-last+warning remains ONLY as a legacy/integrity net, never the designed path. [oracle: filing-path refusal tests]

/cam-plan sources the spec by specSource: "grill" => use the spec field (settled, do-not-re-litigate contract intact); "derived"/"operator" => use title+description as proposed scope (the WHAT is settled, the HOW the planner refines); derivedFrom is passed to subagent-planner which reads the parent issue(s) for context; the auditor Step 8 backstop is unchanged. [oracle: cam-plan.md review + planner-prompt test]

/cam-plan prints an honest non-grilled signal for derived/operator specs (replacing the now-moot stage:idea D2 warning), e.g. "non-grilled spec (specSource: derived, from CAM-NNN); treating description as proposed scope". [oracle: cam-plan.md review]

No content-heuristic auto-marking exists; fast-track is set only via the explicit flags. The structural SUGGESTION auto-filer is explicitly OUT of scope (separate follow-up issue). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The first ADR in docs/adr/ (lazily created) documents this decision: it revises CAM-107 ("grill is the singular human gate"); records that PRD-readiness has two doors; lists alternatives considered (X flag vs Y file-as-specified; binding vs overridable WSJF inheritance; soft vs hard guardrails); and the consequences (speed for derived work + rigor-skip mitigated by hard guardrails, auditor backstop, and explicit-only marking). [oracle: file-assert docs/adr/*.md exists with required sections]

Tests cover: schema conditional validation (specSource/derivedFrom/description), filing-path refusals (unresolvable WSJF; derived without parent), cam-plan spec-sourcing by specSource, and embed/template parity for any shipped-artifact change (cam-plan.md copies + _generated.ts). [oracle: bun test]
Quality gates pass: bun run typecheck, bun test, bun run check:all. [oracle: bun run check:all]
gotchas: specSource MUST be a TOTAL discriminator on specified with absent=>grill back-compat, so the 3 filter sites (select.ts:34 / rank.ts:154 / gate.ts:150) stay byte-untouched (Option Y). Do NOT change the plannability predicate.

WSJF inheritance from derivedFrom is a SUGGESTED DEFAULT (overridable), not a binding copy: a derived fix often has different urgency than its parent (the CAM-143 footgun is more time-critical than the CAM-142 feature that spawned it).
derivedFrom is string[] (a fix can consolidate several parent issues/suggestions), validated via JSON-schema if/then conditional, not a flat required.

The filing path is the CAM-90 writeIssueFile CAS primitive (src/issues/alloc.ts) via createLocalIssueOnMain (src/commands/issue-file.ts); since CAM-142 it syncs the worktree after CAS, so filing fast-track issues will not leave a staged-deletion.

Do NOT edit the vendored grilling/domain-modeling skills; the recommendation-quality clause is CAM-145 and lives in the cam-owned grill-with-docs wrapper + cam-plan Step 6. Keep these two issues separate.
docs/adr/ does not exist yet (created lazily per the project convention); this issue creates it with the first ADR. Follow the 3-gate ADR test already passed during the grill.
domainTerms: plan-readiness (the gate /cam-plan requires; has two doors: grilled or born-ready)
specSource (discriminator on a specified issue: grill | derived | operator)
fast-track (filing an issue directly at stage:specified, bypassing the grill)
derived issue (specSource:derived; a fix/follow-up of one or more parent issues, carries derivedFrom)
operator issue (specSource:operator; a standalone nice-to-have the operator fast-tracks, no parent)
derivedFrom (string[] of parent issue ids; powers WSJF inheritance and provenance audit)
grill-exempt (an issue that reaches plan-readiness without the grill interview)
